name: Opal Green
lede: Opal Green is a dark, saturated bluish green standardized as RAL 6026, named for the gem rather than measured from one.

sections.title: Named for a stone it doesn't match
sections.body:
Our library's only source for this value is RAL Classic, catalog number 6026, a German paint standard founded in 1927, so the hex is an approximate screen reading of a printed color card rather than a photographed gem [1]. [[gem:opal|Opal]] itself rarely shows a solid, saturated green like this one; its color play comes from internal structure, not a single pigment, so the name borrows the stone's reputation more than its look [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[pearl-opal-green]] and [[dark-green-blue]], at Compare [[teal|Teal]], [[viridian|Viridian]] and [[dark-slate-grey|Dark Slate Grey]], other deep, cool standards [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a color within six units of this one in only 7, about 0.03 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest is T. Davies's Ship in Full Sail (1827); the rest date from after 1880, including works by Paul Gauguin and Edvard Munch [2]. With this few matches, nothing here supports a claim about when the color was common beyond the paintings listed [2]. The count is a screen-color match, not a claim of RAL 6026 paint on any canvas [2].
